resources.string: Joint force on forearm: %1$s N downward
Opposing moments at balance: %1$s N·m each
Example assumptions: forearm mass 2.5 kg, centre of mass 16 cm from the elbow, g = 9.8 m/s². Arrows indicate direction, not force magnitude.
B × muscle arm = forearm weight × 0.16 m + load weight × load arm. E = B − forearm weight − load weight. All distances are converted to metres.

Elbow example only: horizontal rigid forearm, vertical forces and a relaxed antagonist. No acceleration, fatigue, co-contraction or personalized geometry. Control ranges are teaching choices, not safe lifting limits. This is not a strength test, injury prediction or rehabilitation prescription; it is not saved as a health measurement.
